705869.t: From Proto-Indo-European *yes- (“to boil, foam”). Compare Sanskrit येषति (yeṣati, “to boil, bubble up”), यसति (yásati, “to froth up, foam”), English yeast.

705879.t: Uncertain. Could be from unattested *ζατός (*zātós), from the same root of δίζημαι (dízēmai, “to seek”), Proto-Indo-European *yeh₂- (“to go, seek”), whence ζῆλος (zêlos, “zeal”) and ζημία (zēmía, “damage, loss”).

705871.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *yeh₂- Proto-Indo-European *-los Proto-Indo-European *yéh₂los Ancient Greek ζῆλος From Proto-Indo-European *yeh₂- (“to go, travel, search, inquire”). Related to Ζητήρ (Zētḗr).

705875.t: From ζηλόω (zēlóō, “to emulate”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

705896.t: Unknown; suggested sources have included Egyptian, Proto-Scythian, Pre-Greek, or a native origin, in which case it would be related to ζύμη (zúmē, “yeast”) and ζέω (zéō, “to boil”).

705865.t: From Proto-Indo-European *yéwgos (“team of yoked animals”). See also ζεύγνυμι (zeúgnumi, “to join”).

705877.t: Sommer connected the word with ζῆλος (zêlos, “fervour, zeal”), ζητέω (zētéō, “to inquire, search, investigate”), and δίζημαι (dízēmai, “to seek out, look for”), based on a breakdown of the word as ζη-μία (zē-mía), which suggests a derivation from…

705895.t: From ζυγόν (zŭgón, “the yoke of a plow or carriage; a crossbar of the lyre”) + -όω (-óō, “verbal suffix”).

705851.t: Fabricated by ancient grammarians as the full form of contracted ζῶ (zô), but this is truly from ζώω (zṓō), from Proto-Hellenic *d͏̌ṓwō, from *gʷyṓwō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷyéh₃woh₂. Doublet of βιόω (bĭóō).
